title: Isaiah Chapter 40 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 40 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 40 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 40.

questions.question: In Isaiah 40, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people
The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness
O Zion, that bringest good tidings
questions.correctAnswer: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people
questions.explanation: This phrase appears in the very first verse of the chapter, Isaiah 40:1.

questions.question: What should be spoken to Jerusalem according to Isaiah 40:2?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:2 states that Jerusalem's warfare is accomplished and her iniquity is pardoned.

questions.question: What is the voice crying in the wilderness to prepare?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:3 mentions preparing the way of the LORD.

questions.question: What will happen to every valley and mountain according to Isaiah 40:4?
options: They shall be exalted and made low
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be exalted and made low
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:4 states that every valley shall be exalted and every mountain and hill shall be made low.

questions.question: What shall be revealed according to Isaiah 40:5?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:5 states that the glory of the LORD shall be revealed.

questions.question: What does the voice say in Isaiah 40:6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:6 states that the voice said, 'Cry.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 40:7, what happens to the grass and the flower?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:7 states that the grass withereth and the flower fadeth.

questions.question: What shall stand forever according to Isaiah 40:8?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:8 states that the word of our God shall stand for ever.

questions.question: What should Zion do according to Isaiah 40:9?
options: Lift up thy voice with strength
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:9 instructs Zion to bring good tidings, lift up her voice with strength, and not be afraid.

questions.question: What will the Lord GOD come with according to Isaiah 40:10?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:10 states that the Lord GOD will come with a strong hand.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 40:11 say about how He will lead His flock?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:11 states that He shall feed His flock like a shepherd.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 40:2, Jerusalem's iniquity is what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:2 states that Jerusalem's iniquity is pardoned.

questions.question: In Isaiah 40:3, a voice cries to prepare the way of the LORD in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:3 confirms that there is a voice crying in the wilderness to prepare the way of the LORD.

questions.question: Every mountain will be exalted according to Isaiah 40:4?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:4 states that every mountain shall be made low, not exalted.

questions.question: The flower of the field will last forever according to Isaiah 40:8?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:8 indicates that the flower fadeth, implying it will not last forever.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 40 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 40 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand?
questions.explanation: The answer is God as mentioned in Isaiah 40:12, which describes His ability to measure the waters.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 40:1 promise will happen if someone comforts God's people as commanded?
options: They will be blessed with riches
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:2 states that comforting Jerusalem leads to her iniquity being pardoned.

questions.question: Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:13 indicates that no one has directed the Spirit of the LORD.

questions.question: To whom does Isaiah 40:18 suggest we compare God?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:18 asks whom we can liken God to, implying that there is nothing comparable to Him.

questions.question: What is said about the nations in Isaiah 40:15?
options: They are like a drop in the bucket
They are the rulers of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: They are like a drop in the bucket
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:15 describes nations as merely a drop in a bucket, emphasizing their insignificance compared to God.

questions.question: Why should we not liken God according to Isaiah 40:19?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:18 and 40:19 emphasize that there is no likeness or image that can adequately represent God.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 40:11 say about God's care for His people?
options: He will feed and gather them
questions.correctAnswer: He will feed and gather them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:11 portrays God as a shepherd caring for His flock, indicating His nurturing role.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 40:22, how does God view the inhabitants of the earth?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:22 compares the inhabitants of the earth to grasshoppers, highlighting God's supremacy.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 40:16 imply about offerings from Lebanon?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:16 states that Lebanon and its beasts are not sufficient for a burnt offering, indicating their inadequacy.

questions.question: What is the nature of the advice given to God in Isaiah 40:14?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:14 highlights that God does not need counsel or instruction, showcasing His wisdom and sovereignty.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 40:8 state about the word of God?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:8 declares that the word of our God will stand forever, emphasizing its eternal truth.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 40:7, what happens to all flesh?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:7 states that all flesh is like grass that withers, illustrating the transient nature of human life.

questions.question: Is it true that all nations are considered as nothing before God according to Isaiah 40:17?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:17 explicitly states that all nations are as nothing before God.

questions.question: Is it false that God requires much to be satisfied according to Isaiah 40:16?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:16 implies that even great offerings from Lebanon are insufficient for Him, indicating His independence from human offerings.

questions.question: Is it false that God's glory will be revealed according to Isaiah 40:5?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:5 promises that the glory of the LORD shall be revealed, indicating that it will indeed be revealed.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 40 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 40.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 40:23, what does God bring to nothing?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:23 states, 'That bringeth the princes to nothing; he maketh the judges of the earth as vanity,' indicating that God brings princes to nothing.

questions.question: In Isaiah 40:24, what happens to those who are 'planted' or 'sown'?
options: They shall wither and be taken away as stubble
They shall grow strong and fruitful
They shall be protected by the Lord
They shall be blessed with abundance
questions.correctAnswer: They shall wither and be taken away as stubble
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:24 says, '...and he shall also blow upon them, and they shall wither, and the whirlwind shall take them away as stubble,' describing the fate of those who are planted or sown.

questions.question: Who is described as the 'Holy One' who asks, 'To whom then will ye liken me?'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:25 states, 'To whom then will ye liken me, or shall I be equal? saith the Holy One,' referring to the LORD.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 40:26, what does God do when He calls the stars?
options: He calleth them all by names
questions.correctAnswer: He calleth them all by names
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:26 says, 'he calleth them all by names by the greatness of his might,' showing God's sovereign knowledge over creation.

questions.question: What complaint does Jacob express in Isaiah 40:27?
options: "My way is hid from the LORD, and my judgment is passed over from my God"
"The mountains have fallen and the hills removed"
questions.correctAnswer: "My way is hid from the LORD, and my judgment is passed over from my God"
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:27 records Jacob saying, 'My way is hid from the LORD, and my judgment is passed over from my God,' expressing a feeling of divine absence.

questions.question: What is promised to those who wait upon the LORD in Isaiah 40:31?
options: They shall renew their strength and mount up with wings as eagles
They shall become rulers over nations
questions.correctAnswer: They shall renew their strength and mount up with wings as eagles
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:31 promises, 'But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chazaq' in Isaiah 40:29 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Chazaq' in Isaiah 40:29 means 'to strengthen or make strong,' as it states, 'He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.'

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 40:6-8 to contrast the transience of humanity and the permanence of God's word?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:6-8 uses parallelism, contrasting 'All flesh is grass' with 'the word of our God shall stand for ever,' a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God giving strength to the weary as found in Isaiah 40:29-31?
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:28-30 echoes Isaiah 40:29-31, offering rest and strength to the weary, fulfilling the Old Testament promise of renewal of strength.

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse connects to the declaration of God's unmatched sovereignty in Isaiah 40:18-25?
questions.explanation: Psalm 113:5-6 speaks of God 'who is enthroned on high' and 'looketh down on the heavens and the earth,' connecting to Isaiah 40's theme of God's unmatched sovereignty.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Isaiah 40:23 in the chapter?
options: Isaiah 40:22, describing God sitting upon the circle of the earth
Isaiah 40:21, asking if people have not heard from the beginning
Isaiah 40:20, about choosing a tree for a graven image
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 40:22, describing God sitting upon the circle of the earth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:22 immediately precedes 40:23 and describes God sitting upon the circle of the earth, setting context for God's sovereignty over princes and judges.

questions.question: What literary technique is employed in Isaiah 40:24's depiction of princes as stubble blown away by the whirlwind?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:24 uses simile, comparing princes to stubble blown away by a whirlwind, emphasizing their frailty and impermanence.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 40:28 describe God's understanding?
options: There is no searching of his understanding
It is limited like man's understanding
It can be measured by human wisdom
It is hidden from all creation
questions.correctAnswer: There is no searching of his understanding
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:28 declares, 'there is no searching of his understanding,' emphasizing God's infinite wisdom beyond human grasp.

questions.question: What typology is expressed in Isaiah 40:11 about the Lord feeding his flock like a shepherd?
options: God as the Good Shepherd caring for His people
The king as a conquering warrior
The prophet as a judge of nations
questions.correctAnswer: God as the Good Shepherd caring for His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:11 typologically presents God as the Good Shepherd, a motif later echoed in John 10:11 where Jesus identifies as the Good Shepherd.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 40:31 promises that those who wait upon the LORD will walk and not faint.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:31 states, 'they shall walk, and not faint,' confirming the promise for those who wait upon the LORD.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 40 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 40 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 40:2 teach about God's forgiveness and judgment?
options: God fully pardons sin after the completion of judgment
God forgives sin without any judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God fully pardons sin after the completion of judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:2 states that Jerusalem's iniquity is pardoned because her warfare is accomplished, indicating that judgment precedes full pardon.

questions.question: What doctrine about the transient nature of human life is taught in Isaiah 40:6?
options: All flesh is like grass and its glory like the flower of the field
All flesh is eternal and unchanging
Human life is insignificant but eternal
Human glory is everlasting and enduring
questions.correctAnswer: All flesh is like grass and its glory like the flower of the field
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:6 clearly teaches the doctrine that human life and glory are transient, like grass and flowers that wither and fade.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providential care for His people is expressed in Isaiah 40:11?
options: God shepherds His people gently and tenderly
God abandons the weak and forsakes the helpless
God cares only for the strong and mighty
questions.correctAnswer: God shepherds His people gently and tenderly
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:11 portrays God feeding His flock like a shepherd, gathering lambs in His arm, and gently leading those with young, emphasizing tender care.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 40:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:12 describes God's incomprehensible power in measuring waters, heavens, dust, mountains, and hills, demonstrating His omnipotence.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Isaiah 40:28?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:28 emphasizes that the everlasting God does not faint or grow weary and that His understanding is unsearchable, highlighting His omnipotence.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 40:3 connect to New Testament themes of redemption?
options: It prefigures John the Baptist’s role preparing the way for Christ
It refers only to Old Testament Israel with no New Testament connection
It prophesies the destruction of Jerusalem without hope
It describes a literal highway for physical travel
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures John the Baptist’s role preparing the way for Christ
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:3’s call to prepare the way of the LORD is quoted in the Gospels as fulfilled by John the Baptist preparing for Jesus’ ministry.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 40:5 relate to the eschatological revelation of God in the New Testament?
options: It anticipates the universal manifestation of God's glory at Christ’s second coming
It denies any future revelation of God’s glory
It only applies to the historical return from exile
It predicts the end of all flesh before God’s glory is revealed
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the universal manifestation of God's glory at Christ’s second coming
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:5 speaks of the glory of the LORD being revealed so all flesh shall see it together, aligning with New Testament eschatology of Christ’s return.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 40:8 and Isaiah 40:6 teach about God’s word and human frailty?
options: The word of God is eternal while human life is transient like grass
Both God's word and human life are fleeting and unreliable
Human life is eternal but God's word fades away
Neither God's word nor human life has lasting value
questions.correctAnswer: The word of God is eternal while human life is transient like grass
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:6 and 40:8 together contrast the fading nature of flesh with the everlasting nature of God's word.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God's sovereignty and human insignificance is taught in Isaiah 40:15 and Isaiah 40:17?
options: Nations and peoples are insignificant before God's sovereign power
God shares sovereign power equally with nations and peoples
Nations have equal power with God
questions.correctAnswer: Nations and peoples are insignificant before God's sovereign power
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:15 and 40:17 emphasize that nations are as a drop of a bucket and less than nothing before God’s sovereign greatness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine creation and providence is taught in Isaiah 40:26 and Isaiah 40:22?
options: God created and sustains the heavens and earth with sovereign control
Creation is independent of God’s will and control
God is limited in creating the heavens and earth
The earth is flat and unmovable
questions.correctAnswer: God created and sustains the heavens and earth with sovereign control
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:22 and 40:26 describe God as creator of the earth and heavens, who calls and names the stars, showing His providential control.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Isaiah 40:21–22 teaches an ancient, incorrect cosmology. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It uses poetic imagery to affirm God's sovereignty over the whole earth and heavens
It insists on a literal flat earth and denies God’s sovereignty beyond Israel
It teaches that God is limited to the earth’s surface
It denies God as creator and sustainer of the universe
questions.correctAnswer: It uses poetic imagery to affirm God's sovereignty over the whole earth and heavens
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:21–22 employs metaphorical language about the 'circle of the earth' and heavens spread like a tent to emphasize God's universal sovereignty, not to teach scientific cosmology.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's exclusive divinity is taught in Isaiah 40:18?
options: God is incomparable and beyond all human likenesses
God is like other gods made by human hands
God can be accurately represented by idols
God is limited to physical forms
questions.correctAnswer: God is incomparable and beyond all human likenesses
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:18 challenges any comparison or likeness to God, affirming His unique, incomparable divine nature.

questions.question: What doctrine about human idolatry is taught in Isaiah 40:19–20?
options: Idolatry is futile and involves human-crafted images that cannot move or save
Idolatry is an acceptable form of worship
Idols have power equal to God
Idolatry is praised as wise and spiritually beneficial
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry is futile and involves human-crafted images that cannot move or save
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:19–20 describes the making of graven images by goldsmiths and craftsmen, highlighting the futility of trusting in idols made by human hands.

questions.question: What doctrine about the renewal of strength through reliance on God is taught in Isaiah 40:31?
options: Those who wait on the LORD will renew their strength and not grow weary
Human strength is sufficient without God
Waiting on God leads to weakness and failure
Strength is unrelated to faith in God
questions.correctAnswer: Those who wait on the LORD will renew their strength and not grow weary
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:31 promises renewal of strength and endurance for those who wait on the LORD, teaching a doctrine of spiritual sanctification and sustenance.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s guidance and judgment is taught in Isaiah 40:13–14?
options: God’s wisdom and judgment are unsearchable and without counsel
God relies on others for counsel and teaching
God’s judgment is fallible and changeable
God is taught by created beings
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wisdom and judgment are unsearchable and without counsel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:13–14 rhetorically questions who could counsel or instruct God, teaching the doctrine of God's perfect, independent wisdom and judgment.
